doc.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024

title: Moving to Georgetown and quitting the dice
summary: His mother moves the family to Georgetown with its new high school, and Griffin stops gambling out of conscience.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: and she said, “You know the reason I left from under the hill, Ethel told me James Richard was down there with the guys gambling.” And when we would gamble we would get a pint of corn whiskey that we knew where the guy who — we wouldn’t do that, we’d get a pint of corn whiskey and but I never drank because I knew my mother could smell it on me and so, but she found me one day gambling. Well she must have came home early. And she never told me. She said, then I said, “When I saw James Richard down there gambling with the guys I knew it was time for me to move.” She moved to a place called Georgetown. And in Georgetown it was — the high school was just built. It was — oh tennis courts, running where you could train, a running track and football and everything. The atmosphere was so changed from day to night. There was no guys gambling, there was no place to have corn whiskey hidden and everything. And I just adapted to that. I went out for football, I trained with the football team, I learned to play tennis and all kinds of stuff. But that was it. And my mother just got me out of that neighborhood into another neighborhood.
Yeah, I’m glad because I might not be talking to you today if you had —

Yeah. If I had stayed under the hill. My father was ready to be put in jail, because — but you know the thing with me, I realized two things with that gambling thing. There was a guy who lived across the street from me, he had a wife and two kids. And he would come, work all week and cash his check and then he would gamble and lose a portion of money and all and I couldn’t — I stopped being in there. I said I can’t do this because I’m taking money out of his wife’s and two kids’ money you know and I didn’t have the heart to do it anymore and I stopped with the crooked dice thing because my heart wasn’t cold enough to do that, to win the money off of him and then see that he didn’t have that money to feed his kids and everything.
